result:
I fixed the README map: `gov accept W2-134` now reads it and reports counts, 21 failed and 7 passed out of 28, instead of `ACCEPT_NO_MAP`. One thing went further than the brief, explained under discoveries: I also renumbered the failure lines to match the ticket.

**Sandbox check:** (a) the write to `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/.sandbox-trial-W2-134` failed with `OSError: [Errno 30] Read-only file system`, as required; (b) `git hash-object -w --stdin` worked (`1ae28402a109…`) and `git update-index --refresh` worked.
**ps check:** nothing of mine. I ran `ps -eo pid,args -C ollama,llama-server`; the `-e` made it list every process the sandbox can see, which was only my shell and `ps` itself, so no ollama or llama-server process is running.

- **task:** W2-134 (DAEO-m4rq), put the README map in the form the acceptance runner reads.
- **status:** DONE
- **work_completed:**
  - Renamed the map's header to `| KPI line | Test (node id) | On this branch | What it checks |`. The old second column, `Case (full node id)`, starts with neither `test` nor `file`, so `parse_map` skipped the whole table.
  - The runner does read several ids in one cell: in `src/gov/accept/runner.py:27`, `JOIN` accepts `,` `/` `;` `and`. So I kept the comma cells as two lines.
  - The runner stops reading a cell at ` (`. So `S1 (with S7)`, `S4 (S7)` and `S6 (F3)` became `S1`, `S4` and `S6`, and their notes ("With S7.", "The review's F3.") now begin the "What it checks" cell.
  - No case, test file or expected state changed.
- **files_changed:** `tests/acceptance/W2-134/README.md` only. Commit `f0c74114d` on `w2/W2-134-tests`.
- **evidence:**
  - Running the runner's own `parse_map` gives success-1 to 6 and failure-1 to 4.
  - `gov accept W2-134 --root /home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/W2-134-tests`, run through the heavy slot, exited 3 (`outcome: fail`, `error_kind: null`), totals passed 7, failed 21, skipped 0, unmapped 0. The README expects exactly 21 red and 7 green.
  - Per line, success-1 to 6 are fail, fail, fail, pass, fail, fail; failure-1 to 4 are fail, pass, fail, fail. Every red line is red because of the S1–S6 reds still there on this branch.
  - I used no TMPDIR scratch beyond the 1-file parse check in the session scratchpad.
- **tests:** I didn't run pytest myself. `gov accept`'s own run had no real-model exclusion flags, and these tests use stand-ins only, so it left nothing out.
- **discoveries:** The README's failure numbers came from before S5 was added, and the ticket has since put the family line first. The ticket now lists F1 = family hit inside a longer token or below the floor, F2 = writes the sets root, F3 = another commit's lines, F4 = unresolved text printed. With the old numbers, the runner would have credited the sets-root guard to the family line. I renumbered to the ticket's order (S1/S2 `F2` → `F3`, S2 `F1` → `F2`, S3 `F3` → `F4`, S5 stays `F1`) and added a short paragraph under the table saying so. Each line still names the same failure line as before, by its text.
- **risks:** If the CTO wanted success ids only, the failure-line rows can be dropped. That would remove failure-1 to 4 from `gov accept`'s report and change nothing else.
- **lessons:** A map's header must have one column starting with `kpi` and one starting with `test` or `file`; any other title makes the runner ignore the table without saying why.
- **proposed_decisions:** none.
- **unresolved:** none.
- **recommended_next_action:** The CTO merges `f0c74114d` into the engineer's branch; the engineer builds and then runs `gov accept W2-134`.

**TESTS-READY:** W2-134's map is readable by `gov accept` (10 lines, 28 items, 21 red and 7 green on this branch, 0 unmapped) at `f0c74114d`.
